claims.text: Thermal oxidation at 600–800°C will increase the thickness of the surface oxide film on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The thermal oxidation pretreatment will improve the continuity and adhesion of the surface oxide film.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a naturally formed, less-controlled oxide layer.
Oxidation is significant during sliding at 600–800°C.
The deliberately formed oxide layer is likely to have a spinel-type composition.
The thickened, continuous oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
The thickened, continuous oxide layer provides mechanical support during sliding.
A well-developed oxide film distributes the applied sliding load more uniformly.
A well-developed oxide film reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact and more uniform load distribution limit friction-induced plastic deformation and subsurface damage.
Improved oxide-scale quality inhibits microcrack initiation and mechanisms leading to premature wear.
Thermally oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have better overall wear resistance than as-deposited coatings during sliding at 600–800°C.
Thermally oxidized coatings will exhibit lower wear-track depth than the baseline coating.
Thermally oxidized coatings will exhibit fewer or smaller plastic zones, cracks, or deformation bands than the baseline coating.
The proposed wear and deformation benefits may not occur at room temperature.
The optimum oxide-film thickness, composition, and microstructure for wear performance are not known.
Coating microstructure and local oxidation kinetics may affect the magnitude of the wear benefit.
